questions.topic: Konjunktiv I in reported speech

questions.topic: Konjunktiv II for polite requests
questions.learningObjective: Soften a request with Konjunktiv II

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

options.text: Could you tell me the price?

options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: Konjunktiv II with a modal softens the request into a polite question. The key is C, "Could you tell me the price?". Option A ("What is the price?") is wrong: uses direct question. Option B ("Tell me the price") is wrong: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes. Option D ("The price is high") is wrong: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out.
questions.hint: Modals in Konjunktiv II soften requests.

questions.topic: Konjunktiv II in a wish

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

answer.exemplar: A wish about the past uses Konjunktiv II of the perfect, often with hätte or wäre, as in if only the truffle had been fresh, expressing regret about a past state.

questions.explanation: Past wishes use Konjunktiv II of the perfect with hätte or wäre. This expresses regret about something that did not happen, as in the recipe note.
questions.hint: Past wishes use hätte or wäre.

options.misconception: selects "The indicative form" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition
mistakes a surface feature of "The past participle" for the governing rule

questions.explanation: Verbs without a simple Konjunktiv II use würde plus infinitive. The key is C, "würde plus infinitive". Option A ("The indicative form") is wrong: selects "The indicative form" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition. Option B ("The infinitive alone") is wrong: uses bare infinitive. Option D ("The past participle") is wrong: mistakes a surface feature of "The past participle" for the governing rule.
questions.hint: No simple form means würde plus infinitive.

options.text: Because the verb takes an accusative object already.

questions.explanation: When the verb already has an accusative object, the reflexive pronoun becomes dative. The key is A, "Because the verb takes an accusative object already". Option D ("Because the tense is past") is wrong: ties case to tense.
questions.hint: Dative reflexive when an accusative object exists.
